# ckbadger LLM Capability Map

Site purpose:

- CKB-native explorer focused on exact on-chain data.

Markdown output convention:

- Explorer pages are scoped by network: `/{network}/...`.
- Any supported network-scoped page URL can be requested as markdown by appending `.md`.
- Response content-type: `text/markdown`.
- Markdown YAML frontmatter includes `buildVersion`.
- Examples:
  - `/mainnet/blocks.md`
  - `/mainnet/blocks/123.md`
  - `/testnet/tx/0xabc...def.md`
  - `/mainnet/charts/transaction-count.md`

Raw output convention:

- Raw format can be requested with:
  - suffix: `.raw`
  - query: `?format=raw`
  - accept: `application/vnd.ckbadger.raw+json`
- Negotiation priority: `query.format` > `path suffix` > `Accept` header.
- Raw profile is selected with query param: `profile=default|debugger`
- `profile=debugger` includes `data.txDebugger.mockTransaction`, compatible with `ckb-debugger --tx-file`.
- `/tx/{hash}.raw` includes `data.txWitness` with witness analyses, script-group lens, and inference.
- Raw `meta` includes `buildVersion`.
- Raw responses include headers: `x-ckbadger-format`, `x-ckbadger-profile`, `x-ckbadger-schema`.

<!-- REGISTERED_PAGE_FORMATS -->

API:

- Shared frontend base: `/api/{network}/v1`
- Direct per-network API base: `/api/v1` on that API's configured port
- JSON API supports blocks, transactions, cells, scripts, tokens, assets/identities, charts, DAO,
  forks, hardfork timeline, and optional crawler network observations.
- Address physical holdings: `/api/{network}/v1/addresses/{addr}/holdings` returns an exact
  current-owner capacity partition, six live-cell classes and four holding-kind counts.
  `/api/{network}/v1/addresses/{addr}/cells?class=dao|token|object|identity|script|plain&limit=50&cursor=...`
  filters before cursor pagination. Identity `heldSinceBlock` traces uninterrupted ownership;
  `createdAtBlock` describes the current cell. Protocol-named `.cell` rights remain separate at
  `/api/{network}/v1/addresses/{addr}/dotcell-names` and add no physical capacity.
- Inventory summary: `/api/{network}/v1/assets/summary` reads canonical counts at its returned
  anchor; `/assets` is a separately refreshed cached listing. Collection composition groups and
  exact live DOB-pending item counts are distinct.
- Token history: `/api/{network}/v1/tokens/{typeHash}/history` supplies complete UTC+8 daily
  capacity/supply, complete weekly transfers and exact mint/burn events. `/distribution` supplies
  same-view concentration and balance buckets; `/holders` includes its own `totalSupply` and
  anchor for exact row shares. `/activity-feed` and `/transactions` expose both paginated layers.
  Issuer is nullable and requires script proof; stored name/symbol/decimals provenance is not
  recorded. Unknown decimals remain raw integer amounts.
- Canonical item evidence: append `/cell-versions`, `/protocol`, `/activity-feed` or
  `/transactions` to `/spore/objects/{id}`, `/assets/objects/items/{id}` (m-NFT), or
  `/assets/identities/{dotbit|bit-cell|did|dotcell}/items/{id}`. Versions are oldest first;
  protocol responses include exact raw bytes, byte spans and lossless decoded values.
  Named identity rights do not imply ownership of the physical cell.
- DOB evidence: `/spore/objects/{id}/genetics` separates the current decoder byte map from
  cached VM traits. The original cached execution binary hash was not recorded.
  `/spore/clusters/{id}/insights` reports complete decoding coverage and exact trait counts;
  `/gallery?traits=<JSON map>&limit=24&cursor=...` filters the entire collection before paging.
  Incomplete decoding does not produce partial whole-collection trait frequencies.
- Cluster current cell: `/spore/clusters/{id}/protocol` uses the canonical live type index;
  `current: null` means no current cluster cell. Item capacity excludes the cluster cell.
  Collection capacity histories return complete UTC+8 dates, an anchor and calendar source;
  history readouts never fill missing values from another response.
- Collection activity and transaction feeds append `/activity-feed` or `/transactions` to
  `/spore/clusters/{id}`, `/assets/objects/{id}` or `/assets/identities/{aliasOrId}`.
  `/assets/identities/did/pds` groups current canonical DID document endpoints; an identity may
  name multiple endpoints. Bitcoin-backed media remains a link, not an embedded remote preview.
- Exact live-cell inventory: `/api/{network}/v1/cells/live-summary`; the three class counters are
  mutually exclusive, `dataBearing` is orthogonal, and `tip.block`/`tip.hash` is locally
  verifiable. The endpoint is a fixed-size point read and returns 503 until a canonical snapshot
  is published.
- Script families and references: `/scripts?role=lock|type` filters before pagination and returns
  full-filter lock-cell code-class totals. `/scripts/{name}` returns registered references,
  observed versions, deployment chronology and custody evidence. A family name, exact `code_hash`/`hash_type`
  reference, binary data hash and outpoint are different identities. `/scripts/lookup` is POST,
  while `/scripts/code-cells` reads exact-reference deployments. Current cells are separately
  available at `/cells/by-script?code_hash=0x…&hash_type=data|type|data1|data2&script_kind=lock|type|both`
  with cursor pagination. Unregistered copies do not acquire registered-family provenance.
- DAO evidence: `/dao/statistics` is the current indexed view; `/dao/evidence` separates phase-0
  deposits, phase-1 withdrawal requests, readiness windows, concentration and header/AR proof.
  `/dao/charts/*` and `/charts/*` are historical chart endpoints; complete-day chart points do not
  stand in for the current DAO inventory.
- Chain switches and upgrades: `/forks`, `/forks/overview`, `/forks/{id}` and `/hardforks` expose
  recorded local reorg events, branch/uncle fate and hardfork chronology. A recorded branch
  adoption can differ from today's canonical branch; uncles are chain history, not a count of this
  node's observed switches.
- Scoped identifier search: `/search?q=block:0x…`, `tx:0x…` or `cell:0x…-index` returns
  `resultType`, `matchKind`, `id` and a canonical page `url`. A missing page plus an empty scoped
  search is limited to those checked local sources. A search error is not proof of absence.
- Error-page cell artwork: `/vessels/snapshot` reads a bounded, anchored sample from at most the
  last 12 indexed blocks, the first 6 transactions per block and the first 4 outputs per
  transaction, capped at 64 live cells. Its `tracked` parameter reports previously visible
  outpoint fates; this is illustrative artwork, not an all-live-cell inventory.
- Optional local CKB L1 peer evidence uses `/api/{network}/v1/network/summary`,
  `/network/distributions`, `/network/history`, `/network/peers`, and
  `/network/peers/{peerId}` (the last four are relative to the same API base). Summary distinguishes
  advertised candidates, same-network reachable, verified retained, and verified unavailable;
  `lastRound.localObserver` preserves the configured node's latest longitudinal evidence and
  `lastRound.directSessionObservations` gives exact observer-/peer-initiated counts for that round.
  The unified peer list also retains direct-session-only peers and sorts by
  `latestPositiveObservedAt`. `crawlerDialState` is separate from the exact
  `participation.{discoveryAdvertised,directSessionObserved,crawlerIdentified}` booleans and
  `sessionInitiators`. `primaryAddr`, `lastAdvertisedAt`, and `lastDialObservedAt` are nullable
  because a positive CKB session need not provide a reusable dial address. Detail exposes
  target-centric advertiser evidence, configured-node `directSessions`, retained dial aliases,
  exact typed address observations, separately labeled active evidence, last crawler verification,
  and Discovery counters. Direct sessions preserve observer peer ID, initiator, first/latest
  observation times/rounds, count, and latest session metadata; their `sessionAddresses` are never
  dial aliases. Advertiser entries preserve alias, first/latest positive
  observation time and completed round, and exact observation count; omission from a later random
  Discovery payload is not negative evidence. The crawler has no listener, sends Discovery
  `GetNodes` v0 with no listen port, unions valid response and announce addresses, and reports
  their message counts separately. Verification means an outbound crawler probe
  received an authenticated same-network CKB Identify. `exhausted` is a scoped completed-round
  observation, never a claim that a peer is globally invalid or offline. History
  count metrics are `verifiedPeers` and `reachablePeers`; the UI pairs them into the disjoint
  same-network-reachable and verified-unavailable stack. The peer list accepts exact state and all
  six typed address-observation filters. Session direction is named from the configured local CKB
  observer's vantage: `observerInitiated` is RPC `get_peers.is_outbound=true`, and
  `peerInitiated` is `false`. RPC session addresses are never promoted to crawler dial aliases.
  Participation, session direction, and crawler dialability are orthogonal; no combination proves
  NAT/firewall status, hosting environment, “home node”, or global reachability. Local RPC session
  evidence is accepted only after the node's genesis hash exactly matches the configured network.
- Capability descriptor: `/capabilities` (formats, profiles, route matrix, and strict error codes).

Notes for agents:

- Prefer markdown pages for narrative + tabular summaries.
- Prefer `/api/{network}/v1` on the shared origin for structured machine extraction and
  full-fidelity fields.
- Use markdown page query params for pagination when supported: `limit`, `cursor`.
